word.name: concept-slug-unique
word.title: Concept Slug Unique
word.description: No two of this instance's own concepts share a slug or a key.

graphRule.name: concept-slug-unique
graphRule.says: no two of this instance's own concepts share a slug or a key. This is BIBLE §10's rule 10, as its full text gives it (tapestry-cli `docs/NORMALIZATION.md`, 2026-03-23): within one author's graph, because a concept's key, `oKeys.singular`, is what its elements' JSON is filed under (`{"dog": {…}}`). A concept is this instance's own when its header's author is the instance's assistant, with a letter or without one. Another author's concept with the same slug is expected, and isn't a violation: the Grapevine settles which one counts (rule 8). Names aren't part of the rule; no rule makes them unique.
graphRule.kind: a graph rule, about the owner's and the admins' own concepts (D4).
graphRule.check: the same `violations` over every own concept, each as `{ concept }`, names each concept that shares a slug or a key with another, both of the pair. `rules check` (A10.31) will run it over the graph.
graphRule.repair: none yet. A slug clash is fixed with `graph update-concept --slug`. A key clash needs a concept moved to another key, which no operation does yet.
graphRule.enforcedBy: the guards of `graph create-concept` and `graph update-concept`, run again after each takes its lock, so two writes at once can't both pass it. The rule's code is in `src/operations/rules/concept-slug-unique.js`. Built in story graph-operations-first-slice #16 (ADR 0016).

code.summary: No two of this instance's own concepts share a slug or a key (BIBLE §10, rule 10)

refusals.when: A slug another of this instance's own concepts has; the refusal names it
A name whose key another of this instance's own concepts has under another slug; the refusal names it
